findings.claim: The plan requires crash durability evidence for both Postgres and Surreal but only defines a Postgres persistence supplement, leaving Surreal durability unowned.
findings.evidence: The plan states: "Postgres and Surreal each need the crash suite." The certification coverage matrix later lists only "Postgres persistence supplement | `cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features server-full,postgres-backend --test a2a_thread_service`" and contains no corresponding Surreal supplement or command.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Surreal persistence certification row and execution-map ownership with the exact feature flags, fixture setup, crash-boundary coverage, evidence directory, and completion gate; make phase completion block on both Postgres and Surreal crash receipts.

findings.claim: The final governed-evaluation task claims to run Tier 2 and the separate Tier 3 milestone, but its bound verification command covers only one Rust test, so the executable gate can pass without the required completion checks.
findings.evidence: The plan says "execution-map.json binds all 44 tasks to files, fixtures, outputs and all 85 scenarios" and lists Tier 2 commands: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features server-full`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm -C frontend test:coverage`, plus Tier 3 as the separate `runtime-harness-profile-certification` milestone. But execution-map task `harness-governed-evaluation` `3.1` is titled "Run phase Tier 2 checks after units complete and separately execute the registered local Tier 3 milestone when eligible" while its `verification` array contains only `cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features server-full --test harness_governed_evaluation`.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind task 3.1 to the full Tier 2 command set and to an explicit required Tier 3 milestone receipt check, or split the Tier 2 and Tier 3 gates into separate tasks with non-ambiguous commands and artifacts.
